title: Tray, soil, a piece of turf or grass, plastic sheet, measuring jug, 200 ml of water, a book to tilt the tray
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y7 lesson 18 (Tray, soil, a piece of turf or grass, plastic sheet, measuring jug, 200 ml of water, a book to tilt the tray)
intro: Lesson 18: How we use rivers; floods on the Thames; home fieldwork. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.title: Sort into: Physical cause / Human cause
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Physical cause, Human cause.
blocks.answer: Physical cause: heavy rain; saturated soil; snowmelt. Human cause: concrete car parks; deforestation; building on flood plains

panels.title: Thames floods
points: 1953: North Sea storm surge; over 300 deaths in England

model.title: Fair test: which surface has the most run-off?

parts.text: Tilt a tray at the same angle each time
Cover with soil, grass turf, then a plastic sheet
Collect and measure run-off in a jug
Repeat three times; find the mean

keywords.def: when a river overflows its banks
the volume of water flowing in a river, in cumecs
flat land by a river that floods

questions.q: Explain how building on a flood plain increases flood risk. (2 marks)
questions.a: Concrete and tarmac are impermeable (1), so rain runs off quickly into the river, raising discharge (1)

questions.q: Core: Plan your home run-off fieldwork on the sheet: question, hypothesis, equipment, method, results table. Carry it out this week with an adult.
questions.a: Complete plan with a fair test and results table

questions.q: Extend: Explain two uses of the Thames.
questions.a: For example: water supply for London; transport and trade via the Port of London

questions.q: Stretch: Why did the 1953 flood come from the sea, not the river?
questions.a: A storm surge pushed sea water up the estuary

questions.q: Which surface will give most run-off?
questions.a: C) Plastic sheet. Plastic is impermeable, so no water infiltrates.

questions.q: Big question: natural or human disaster?
questions.a: Both: heavy rain is natural, but building and paving increase run-off and risk
